newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRANCE RECORD LACKLUSTRE 1-0 WIN OVER SWEDEN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRANCE RECORD LACKLUSTRE 1-0 WIN OVER SWEDEN.

text.p: France recorded an unconvincing 1-0 victory over Sweden at the Parc des Princes on Wednesday in their last friendly before launching their campaign for the 1998 soccer World Cup.
A penalty from Internazionale striker Youri Djorkaeff shortly before the break was all the French could manage as they put on another lacklustre performance in front of goal.
The result was all the more fortunate as the penalty, awarded by Belgian referee Markus Sandra for a foul on Djorkaeff by Sweden's veteran goalkeeper Thomas Ravelli, looked very generous.
Otherwise, the best chances on a warm night in Paris fell to the Swedes.

Martin Dahlin had a fine opportunity to open the scoring with a header in the 20th minute and goalkeeper Fabien Barthez twice had to intervene at the feet of Kennet Anderson after blunders in his defence.
French manager Aime Jacquet has had problems in attack since his side lost in the semifinals of the European championship last June.
He obviously has not found the answers yet ahead of next June's Tournoi de France, involving Brazil, England and Italy.
